fidelity: F2a — Point Reactor Kinetics coupled to Lumped Fuel/Graphite/Helium Thermal Model
source: Duderstadt & Hamilton (1976) Nuclear Reactor Analysis, Wiley; Hetrick (1971) Dynamics of Nuclear Reactors; Zhang et al. (2009) Nucl. Eng. Des. 239:2265 (HTR-PM); Dong (2011) Nucl. Eng. Des. 241:4755; Reitsma (2004) IAEA TRS-424; Strydom (2013) Nucl. Eng. Des. 263:516 (PBMR neutronics)

unit.name: Generic 250 MWth Pebble-Bed HTGR (HTR-PM / PBMR class), TRISO-fueled, helium-cooled

Lambda_neutron_s.note: Prompt neutron generation time; large in graphite-moderated thermal reactor (well-thermalized spectrum, long diffusion path) ~1 ms (Duderstadt 1976; Strydom 2013)

beta_total.note: Total delayed neutron fraction for U-235 thermal fission (Duderstadt 1976 Table)

lambda_i_per_s.note: 6-group delayed neutron precursor decay constants, U-235 (Keepin/Duderstadt 1976)

alpha_fuel_pcm_per_K.note: Fuel (Doppler) temperature reactivity coefficient; strongly negative, prompt, dominant in TRISO/UO2 fuel (Reitsma 2004; Strydom 2013)

alpha_graphite_pcm_per_K.note: Graphite moderator temperature reactivity coefficient; negative, slow (acts through large graphite thermal mass)

M_fuel_t.note: Fuel+pebble matrix effective mass that holds fission heat (TRISO kernels + SiC + graphite matrix of fuel spheres)

cp_fuel_J_per_kgK.note: Effective specific heat of graphite-matrix fuel pebbles (graphite-dominated)

cp_graphite_J_per_kgK.note: Graphite specific heat at HTGR operating temperature (~700C); ~1.3-1.9 kJ/kgK

M_helium_kg.note: Helium coolant inventory in core/primary loop

cp_helium_J_per_kgK.note: Helium specific heat (monatomic ideal gas, 5R/2M), essentially constant

hA_fuel_graphite_MW_per_K.note: Fuel-to-graphite conductance (fission heat conducted from kernels into moderator/structure)

mdot_helium_kg_per_s.note: Helium mass flow rate at rated power (HTR-PM ~96 kg/s)

T_helium_inlet_C.note: Helium core inlet temperature at rated power

T_helium_outlet_C.note: Helium core outlet temperature at rated power

decay_heat_frac.note: Fission-product decay heat as fraction of operating power shortly after shutdown (~6.5%, ANS-5.1); enables passive decay-heat removal
